title: Sensor alert location lookup interpolates raw text into GUID filter -- same pattern as CR-0241
detail: Line 159: `/${EntitySets.properties}?$filter=dcfg_propertyid eq ${locId}&...` -- locId comes from `rd.dcfg_location_id_text` (line 153), which could be a non-GUID value (sensor device friendly name). If non-GUID, filter generates `dcfg_propertyid eq GroupHome-12` -> 400. Same pattern as SensorBanner CR-2026-04-09-0241. Also N+1: one apiGet per unique location id in the current poll, in sequence.
evidence: Operations.jsx:153-168 sensor alert location resolution loop.
recommendedFix: Same fix as CR-0241 -- validate locId against GUID regex before issuing the filter. Also batch the unresolved IDs into a single `$filter=dcfg_propertyid in (...)` query instead of Promise.all individual calls.

title: fetchSensorAlerts outer `catch {}` silently swallows all errors on every 30s poll
detail: Lines 169-171: bare `catch { }` with a comment 'Sensor table may not be available -- fail silently'. Fires every 30 seconds. Any post-deploy regression to dcfg_sensor_readings access or shape is invisible. Parallel to SensorBanner's CR-0242 bare catch.
recommendedFix: Same fix as CR-0242 -- add a module-level flag to log the warning once, then stay silent on subsequent polls.

title: fetchWorkOrders fetches up to 1000 work orders then N+1 queries for unresolved location names
detail: Line 200: `$top=1000` fetches all work orders. Lines 204-216: for every unresolved location ID, a separate apiGet fires `$filter=dcfg_upkeep_location_id eq '${locId}'`. With 50 unique unresolved locations this is 50 sequential API calls on each 2-minute poll. The locationMapRef cache mitigates repeat polls, but the first load can be very slow.
evidence: Operations.jsx:200-216 -- Promise.all of individual location lookups.
recommendedFix: Batch unresolved location IDs into a single OData `$filter=dcfg_upkeep_location_id in (...)` query (Dataverse supports `in` for string fields). Alternatively, resolve location names server-side via a flow or view that joins work items to properties.

title: Work order location resolution has bare catch {} -- individual resolution failures invisible
detail: Line 210: `} catch {}` in the per-location resolution loop inside fetchWorkOrders. If a single location lookup fails (e.g. permissions), it silently returns null with no diagnostic. Since this runs inside the work order polling loop, repeated failures across polls are completely invisible.
evidence: Operations.jsx:210 -- bare catch in work order location resolution.
recommendedFix: Add a console.warn with the failed locId for diagnostic purposes: `catch(e) { console.warn('[Operations] location resolve failed for', locId, e); }`.
